title: Calibrate every promised feasible mean by a terminating finite-bit search
statement: Enumerate positive rational vectors lambda in increasing total binary length. For each, use the already paid SAME-class DDB1/secant moment reduction at accuracy epsilon/8. Return the first whose rational estimate is within strict epsilon/2 of m in sup norm; its TRUE entire-law error is<5epsilon/8. Existence with a stricter margin ensures an accepted candidate eventually occurs, so every promised feasible input terminates. Every individual test is deterministic finite-bit work; the number/height of preceding candidates is NOT polynomially bounded. This is a complete computability result, not the requested efficient general inverse compiler. The full P3 moment proof uses q>=Pr(Pois(lambda)=x0), a polynomial-bit tail U, h=delta/[16(U+2)^2] and two additive-delta*h/16 value calls on the SAME actual class. No Gamma-e_i=Gamma(x0-e_i) identification is used.
